To: docs/climate-programme/border-revenues-launch/handover
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Handover - CBAM launch, Thursday 26 November (draft)

Inês,

I know this is not the handover either of us wanted, and I am sorry. I found the error this afternoon and I am on a train tonight, so what follows is me trying to hand over a launch that is in good shape, wrapped around a mess I created. The mess is mine. Figure 3 was my error, not yours, and if anyone asks on Thursday, say exactly that.

I trust you completely. You ran the annex B runs yourself, you know this paper better than most people alive, and you are better live than you think you are. In Lisbon you rescued my panel when the projector died and nobody watching would have guessed you were improvising. I am not saying that to be nice. I am saying it because you are going to walk in on Thursday and be more than good enough, and I would rather you heard it from me than spent two days wondering.

One line on why I am away, and then we stay on the work: my father is ill, I am with my family. Nothing more than that.

1. WHAT THE LAUNCH IS

Launch of "Who Pays at the Border? CBAM revenues and the least developed countries". Host: MEP Katarina Lindqvist. European Parliament, Altiero Spinelli building, room booked by her office.

2. NEW TIMINGS (Tomás, 23 November)

- Final names of everyone from our side to Tomás by Wednesday 12:00. Security will not admit people who are not on the list.
- Thursday: guests at the security entrance by 12:00, badges collected by Tomás, light lunch outside the room from 12:00.
- 12:30 welcome by Lindqvist (5 min).
- 12:35 presentation, 15 minutes, you. It was 20.
- 12:50 panel: Abena Owusu-Mensah (Accra Trade Policy Centre, remote), Florian Kessler (Alliance of European Steel Users), you. Moderated by Lindqvist.
- Lindqvist has a vote moved into her Thursday lunchtime and must leave at 13:30. She wants at least two questions herself before she goes.
- 13:40 Q&A, 14:00 close.

What this means for you: 15 minutes with a 14-slide deck (v4) is tight. Cut to about ten slides, leave the annex out of the room, and time yourself once before Wednesday. The revenue chart is slide 9 and the summary is slide 6, and both need fixing anyway, so fix them before you rehearse and not after. My speaker notes are still in the deck; rewrite them in your own words, you will speak faster from your own pages.

Also build the panel so the MEP's two questions land early. If she has to go at 13:30, let her have them in the first ten minutes of the panel. That protects the shape of the discussion and it stops you inheriting a half-finished Q&A.

3. THE NUMBER - READ THIS PART TWICE

Correct: 2030 LDC-relevant CBAM revenue is EUR 1.4 billion. Not EUR 2.1 billion. The 2.1 came from a run before the free-allocation phase-out was applied. I got it wrong.

Already fixed: PDF v7 on the drive is corrected (pages 3, 14, 15). Nothing to do there, just make sure it is the version in everybody's hands.

Not fixed:

a) Deck v4, slides 6 and 9, still say 2.1. Correct them, save as v5, use v5 on Thursday. Do this first, it takes twenty minutes and half the rest depends on it.
b) The press release. Hanna sent it to our 34 Brussels contacts on Friday under embargo until Thursday 10:00 CET, and it says 2.1 in the headline and the body. It has to be corrected and re-sent before the embargo lifts. Hanna owns the release; Geert can sign off a corrected version if she wants a senior name on it. Ask Hanna for the contact list and whether anyone has already opened it. Journalists on embargo do read early, and I would rather we tell them than they find it.
c) Anything else that repeats the number: search the folder, website drafts, the newsletter, the abstract I used for the Lisbon side event, the Halvorsen grant report template, any social copy. Over-checking is cheaper than a caption.

Suggested wording for the correction note, for Hanna to send:

"Please replace the 2030 figure in the attached release and the report link. The correct LDC-relevant revenue estimate is EUR 1.4 billion, not EUR 2.1 billion; the earlier figure came from a run before the free-allocation phase-out was applied. The report PDF (v7) is attached and supersedes all earlier versions. No other findings change."

If it comes up in the room or in a call, do not get clever: "The figure was corrected on 23 November, before the launch, and the error was mine." That is the whole answer, and it is the right one. The conclusion of the paper does not change, only the headline number.

4. THE PANEL, AND KESSLER

Florian has signalled in writing that he will raise the 80% pass-through assumption and the resource-shuffling risk, so he will do it whether or not we give him the space. The thing to avoid is letting him frame the paper as optimistic, because then every later question becomes a debate about his number rather than about ours.

Anchors to hold:

- 80% pass-through is the central case, not a best case. Annex B runs 40% and 60%. The result holds at 60% and weakens at 40%. Say it in that order: central case, then sensitivity, then what it does and does not change.
- Resource shuffling: we agree it is a risk, it is in section 5.2, and we recommend the Commission's monitoring report as the way to watch it. Agreeing early with a fair criticism is worth more than defending against it.
- Abena will probably back us on the LDC side, she was strong on the call. Give her room.

Practical bit: you ran those annex B runs yourself, so if Kessler pushes on 60% or 40% you are the person in the room who knows them cold, and you do not need the slides for it. If the clock gets tight, offer to follow up with him and the AESU members after the launch. That is a normal thing for a researcher to offer, and it takes the heat out of the room.

5. ORDER OF WORK

Tonight or first thing tomorrow:
1. Fix deck v4 slides 6 and 9, save as v5.
2. Search everything else for "2.1" and "2,1" (folder, web, newsletter, Lisbon abstract, grant template, social).
3. Get Hanna moving on the corrected release and the note to the 34 contacts, and tell her Geert can sign off if she needs a senior name.
4. Ask Hanna what the two journalists actually asked when they requested a call.

Wednesday 25 November:
5. Badge list to Tomás by 12:00. Final names of everyone from our side who is coming, including Lucy's colleague.
6. 14:00 and 15:00 press calls, trade newsletter and a Belgian daily. Hanna told both of them I would be available Wednesday afternoon. I cannot do them. Take them yourself, or ask Hanna to move them to Thursday morning after the embargo lifts at 10:00. Either is fine, but do not simply leave them hanging, and if you take them, lead with the corrected figure rather than correcting it live. Have PDF v7 open in front of you.
7. Timing run of the 15-minute presentation. Check the Abena remote link.

Thursday 26 November:
8. 10:00, embargo lifts, corrected release goes out.
9. 12:00 guests at security, badges from Tomás, light lunch outside the room from 12:00.
10. 12:30 welcome, 12:35 your presentation, 12:50 panel, 13:30 the MEP leaves after her two questions, 13:40 Q&A, 14:00 close.
11. Somebody from our side takes two photos of the event and notes the attendance numbers. Lucy Tran at the Halvorsen Foundation wants both, ideally by 4 December. Do not let this fall on the day; ask who is doing it on Wednesday.

Two small ones: Abena is remote and her link is in the calendar invite, but test it from the room and find the AV desk in the building before she joins, with a phone dial-in as backup. And make sure somebody eats lunch, including you.

6. IF YOU NEED ME

Call before 09:00 tomorrow and I will pick up. After 09:00 I may not be able to; leave me a message and I will come back to it. If it is genuinely urgent and I am not answering: Geert for sign-off, Hanna for press, and for anything about the numbers the paper and you are the authority. You do not need me to check anything.

7. LAST THING

You are going to be better at this than I would have been on a good day, and I would not have said that in front of the team. If something goes sideways on Thursday, it is a launch, not a verdict on the paper. The paper holds.

Take it and run it. Ring me if anything above is unclear.

Marieke

Subject: On the train - what I still need to do

Before I share the handover draft:

- Re-check the timings against Tomás's email. The MEP leaves at 13:30 and takes two questions first, presentation is 15 minutes, panel starts 12:50. If I have that wrong in the page, fix it before Inês reads it.
- Find out who is actually coming from our side, including Lucy's colleague, so Tomás gets the names by Wednesday 12:00.
- Tell Hanna tonight or first thing that I cannot do the Wednesday 14:00 and 15:00 calls, and that the release needs correcting before Thursday 10:00. Geert can sign off. I do not want that sitting still because I am on a train.
- The 2.1 mistake is mine and the page says so. Leave it in.

For anything anyone asks about why I am away: "my father is ill, I am with my family." Nothing beyond that, and change nothing in writing.

The family wants to talk to me tomorrow morning at 9, so after that I may not pick up. Before 9 I will.

Do not mention the 2027 funding gap to anyone until Geert has spoken to the team in December. It is in my personal notes only.
